exposure: Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal vs. induced/caesarean section)
EO-PE delivering preterm vs. Normotensive delivering at term
cohort: 399 pregnant women (199 with EO-PE delivering preterm and 200 normotensive delivering at term)
finding: Hyper-homocysteinemia is associated with a three-fold increased risk of early onset pre-eclampsia (EO-PE) and is linked to dysregulation of IL-10 and IL-17, potentially impacting mode of delivery.
mod_finding: The association between altered homocysteine metabolism and high IL-10 levels in EO-PE was more pronounced in spontaneous vaginal deliveries compared to induced or caesarean section deliveries.
